column3: “The marauding band” is rendered “the band of men,” and “the former” as “the older sons.”
The Hebrew reads forty-two years; NASB reads twenty-two, as in 2 Kings 8:26. “Daughter” is rendered “granddaughter.”
“In their counsel” is rendered “according to their counsel.”
The Hebrew has “Azariah” for the king of Judah; NASB reads “Ahaziah,” as in 2 Kings 8:29. The opening of the clause about the wounds is unclear in Hebrew.
“Downfall” is rendered “destruction,” and “to Jehu” as “against Jehu.”
“Entered into judgment” is rendered “was executing judgment,” “officials” as “princes,” and “serving” as “ministering to.”
NASB supplies “So there was no one”; “retain strength for kingship” is rendered “retain the power of the kingdom.”
“The offspring of royalty” is rendered “the royal offspring.”
“The chamber of the beds” is rendered “the bedroom”; NASB reorders the clauses and uses parentheses. “She did not kill him” is rendered “so that she would not put him to death.”
